lines.trans: Hyung, did you fight with my sister? She texted me earlier to look for a short-term two-room monthly rental.
If she seriously meant to rent a two-room place she would call a real-estate office herself—why tell me?
Come on, stop acting like an amateur—she obviously meant for me to pass that message on to you!
Meaning she is upset enough to move out, so stop her or handle it yourself!
What is this talk about a two-room rental—is this really something to go this far over?
I told you earlier—since I caused the accident, I am cleaning up the aftermath myself.
You call moving out cleaning up the aftermath?
I am doing it so you will not feel uncomfortable.

examples.trans: Do you fight with your younger sibling often?
Don't fight with each other and get along.

examples.trans: If you really want variety, I will look into others. But not that show.

examples.trans: I should leave. We cannot communicate at all. Go look for another cast member.

meanings.note: Short for 문자 메시지.

examples.trans: I sent a text message.
Why aren't you replying to my text?

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken intensifier; can also function as a noun meaning 'the real thing'.

examples.trans: I'm really busy today.
Is that really delicious?

meanings.note: noun thought

examples.trans: Good idea.
Come to mind.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.note: reflexive pronoun referring back to the subject

examples.trans: You have to look after your own rice bowl.
Do your own work yourself.
A professional salary cannot beat real estate.
The topic of real estate came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: The person called is marked with 에게 or 한테 (e.g., 친구한테 전화하다).

examples.trans: Please call me when you arrive.
I'll call right now.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb.

examples.trans: Why are you running?
Why were you late today?

이러다.gloss: to do this, to act like this

meanings.en: to do this, to act like this
meanings.note: Contracted from 이러하다.

examples.trans: Why are you acting like this?
Please don't do this.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 왜 이래요 아마추어처럼, 형한테 전해달라 이거잖아!
examples.trans: Come on, stop acting like an amateur—she obviously meant for me to pass that message on to you!

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 왜 이래요 아마추어처럼, 형한테 전해달라 이거잖아!
examples.trans: Come on, stop acting like an amateur—she obviously meant for me to pass that message on to you!
This expression comes from 'pass the word along'.

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun for something near the speaker; often contracted to 이거 in speech.

examples.trans: Did you film this too?
How much is this?

meanings.en: a lot, much, in large quantity
meanings.note: Adverbial form of 많다 (to be many/much)

examples.trans: I did a lot of work today.
Please eat plenty and enjoy.

examples.text: 내가 열받아서 그냥 나오지 마라 그랬더니 진짜 안 나오려나 봐.
examples.trans: I lost my temper and told her not to come out, and now she really might skip it.

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 열받다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (lost my temper and).

나가다.gloss: to go out, to step outside

meanings.en: to go out, to step outside, to leave a room
meanings.note: 나- ('out') + 가다 ('to go')

examples.trans: Let's step outside for a moment and talk.
He went out of the conference room.
I want to must catch right now.
How about trying to must catch together tomorrow?
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a noun in questions

examples.trans: What kind of music are you listening to right now?
Is something the matter?

meanings.note: in expressions like 뭔 소리야? ('what are you talking about?')
audible sound made by people or things

examples.trans: Suddenly a strange sound was heard.

examples.text: 말도 안 되는 소리 하지 마.
examples.trans: Don't talk nonsense.

meanings.note: Adverbial form of 이렇다.
Used to emphasize degree.

examples.trans: You can do it like this.
Why is it so cold today?

meanings.note: Sino-Korean numeral used with counters and in numbers

examples.trans: Let's meet in the first-floor lobby.

meanings.note: Used in idioms like 사고를 치다 (to cause trouble).

examples.trans: I caused trouble.
I caused trouble. (2)

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 사고는 내가 쳐놓고 뒷수습은 너더러 하라는 꼴이었으니까, 조만간 뒷수습도 내가 할게.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (det).

불편하다.gloss: to be uncomfortable; to be inconvenient

meanings.en: to be uncomfortable; to be inconvenient
meanings.note: Describes physical discomfort, awkwardness, or inconvenience.

examples.trans: This chair is a bit uncomfortable.
Please let me know if anything is uncomfortable.

meanings.note: Auxiliary verb used after -지 to tell someone not to do something. Ending with -고 (말고) gives a brisk, trailing command. RR: malda.

examples.trans: Please do not worry.
Do not be late, and come early.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

meanings.note: Used before adjectives or verbs.

examples.trans: Please give me a little more.
It's further away.

meanings.note: Often used directly without a locative particle to mean 'here'.

examples.trans: Please sit here.
Here is our office.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 내가 여기 있는 것도 불편한 건 마찬가지지!
examples.trans: Staying here feels just as uncomfortable for me too!

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun referring to something near the listener or already mentioned. Routinely spoken as 그거. RR: geugeot; spoken geugeo.

examples.trans: That is my mobile phone.
That is really important.

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.en: to be like that, to be so
meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그러면.

examples.trans: Then let's meet tomorrow.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
